issues.title: Rank-dependent performance comparison

failure_location.quote: In addition, numerical results validate that the proposed methods indeed converge to stationary points, and the rfGRAP-R method performs better than the GRAP-R method due to the simpler rank-decreasing mechanism.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First, we observe that the GRAP-R method is comparable to other candidates. Second, the rfGRAP and rfGRAP-R methods require more iterations than other candidates, since they only adopt partial information from the tangent cone to avoid retraction.
Second, the rfGRAP-R method is comparable to the TRAM method and performs better than the GRAP-R method since the rfGRAP-R method requires fewer rank-decreasing attempts than the GRAP-R method.

issues.failure_explanation: The contribution sentence claims without qualification that rfGRAP-R performs better than GRAP-R. The old true-rank discussion instead reports that rfGRAP-R requires more iterations than the other candidates, while only the over-estimated-rank discussion explicitly says that rfGRAP-R performs better because it makes fewer rank-decreasing attempts. Thus the old evidence supports a regime-dependent ordering, not unconditional superiority.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory performance summary materially overstates rfGRAP-R's empirical advantage, although the algorithms and convergence results are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unconditional performance comparison with the regime-dependent conclusion already supported by the numerical section: rfGRAP-R requires more iterations in the true-rank experiments, whereas its advantage over GRAP-R is observed for over-estimated ranks because it makes fewer rank-decreasing attempts. No algorithmic or convergence statement needs modification.
issues.why_classification: The true-rank setting is a natural, explicitly tested regime in which the unconditional superiority claim is unsupported, so the repair meaningfully withdraws part of a coherent empirical claim rather than merely clarifying notation. Nevertheless, the old experimental discussion directly supplies a comparable regime-dependent replacement through a contained prose edit, with no new experiment or proof architecture. This is limited rather than major mathematical loss.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: In practice, if the prescribed rank is exactly the true rank of a dataset, the GRAP-R method performs better than the rfGRAP-R method. If the rank is over-estimated or the rank parameter becomes large, the rfGRAP-R method performs better than GRAP-R, since the retraction-free property is able to reduce the computational cost by avoiding exhaustive exploration of multiple lower-rank candidates.

issues.title: Mode-product matrix dimensions

failure_location.quote: The $k$-mode product of a tensor $\tensX$ and a matrix $\mata\in\mathbb{R}^{n_k\times M}$ is denoted by $\tensX\times_k\mata\in\mathbb{R}^{n_1\times\cdots\times M\times\cdots\times n_d}$, where the $ (i_1,\dots,i_{k-1},j,i_{k+1},\dots,i_d)$-th entry of $\tensX\times_k\mata$ is $\sum_{i_k=1}^{n_k}x_{i_1\dots i_d}a_{ji_k}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old declaration gives the multiplying matrix n_k rows and M columns. But j is the new mode index, the entry formula uses a_{j i_k}, and the unfolding X_(k) has n_k rows, so the product A X_(k) requires A to have M rows and n_k columns. Both displayed constructions are therefore undefined in general when M differs from n_k.
issues.overall_effect: The mode-product contract and subsequent nonsquare mode products are literally ill-typed. The intended convention remains unambiguous and is restored everywhere by the same local correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the matrix type in the mode-product definition from A in R^{n_k by M} to A in R^{M by n_k}, and read all subsequent mode products under that corrected convention. Leave the entry formula, unfolding identity, and dependent arguments unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The output index j has range M, the contracted index i_k has range n_k, and the displayed identity (X times_k A)_(k) = A X_(k) uniquely forces A to have M rows and n_k columns. The subsequent mathematics already uses that convention, so an adept reader can make one transcriptional correction without repairing any inference or changing any result.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The $k$-mode product of a tensor $\tensX$ and a matrix $\mata\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times n_k}$ is denoted by $\tensX\times_k\mata\in\mathbb{R}^{n_1\times\cdots\times M\times\cdots\times n_d}$
